item.title: Tenda CVE-2026-11405 Backdoor, DEBULL M365 Phishing, GitHub Workflow Leaks, KDDI Breach
item.content:encoded:
DEBULL Tooling Abuses Microsoft Device-Code Flow to Target M365 Accounts — Must Read

A Microsoft 365 phishing campaign is using DEBULL tooling to abuse Microsoft’s legitimate device-code login flow, tricking users into granting attackers session tokens without fake login pages or password theft. The activity shows Storm-2372-style techniques being packaged into reusable phishing-as-a-service infrastructure for account takeover, data theft, and BEC operations.

  • ZeroBEC observed a Microsoft 365 device code phishing campaign between the last week of June 2026 and early July that used collaboration-themed lures to take control of victim accounts.
  • The campaign used malicious collaboration-style lures to push users into the legitimate Microsoft device login experience while a backend broker generated and polled Microsoft Authentication Broker device-code tokens.
  • ZeroBEC assessed that the activity strongly overlaps with Microsoft’s Storm-2372 reporting from February 2025, but that the operators are using a reusable tooling layer called DEBULL.
  • ZeroBEC said DEBULL is likely a phishing-as-a-service platform that uses GraphSpy or a GraphSpy-derived workflow for Microsoft 365 and Entra post-exploitation.
  • Cisco Talos identified an ARToken phishing-as-a-service operator panel that shares infrastructure, API contracts, and operational patterns with the EvilTokens device code phishing platform.

Major Japanese telco says cyberattack exposed 12 million emails — Must Read

KDDI said a cyberattack on a third-party email platform used by five Japanese ISPs exposed more than 12.2 million email addresses and 7.6 million passwords. The company patched the exploited flaw and affected providers are enforcing password resets.

  • KDDI said a cyberattack on an email platform it operates for internet service providers exposed more than 12.2 million customer email addresses and 7.6 million passwords.
  • The breach affected an email system used to manage customer email accounts, webmail services, and email storage for five Japanese internet service providers.
  • KDDI said attackers exploited a vulnerability in third-party software used by the email platform, and the company patched the flaw and modified the system after detecting the intrusion.
  • KDDI said its own consumer email services for mobile and fixed-line internet customers run on separate infrastructure and were not affected.
  • Affected internet service providers are working to complete mandatory password resets in the coming days.

Hidden backdoor in Tenda router firmware grants admin access — Should Read

Multiple Tenda router firmware versions contain an undocumented authentication backdoor that can grant admin access to the web management panel if the hidden password is known. No patch is available, so users should disable remote web management and limit local exposure.

  • A hidden authentication backdoor has been found in multiple Tenda router firmware versions that could allow an attacker to gain administrative access to the device's web management panel.
  • CERT/CC says CVE-2026-11405 is caused by an undocumented authentication mechanism in the login() function of the /bin/httpd web server binary.
  • If standard MD5-based authentication fails, the firmware checks the plaintext password supplied by the remote user against the sys.rzadmin.password configuration value and grants administrator access if it matches, regardless of the username entered.
  • The issue affects specific firmware versions for the Tenda FH1201, W15E, AC10, AC5, and AC6 V2 routers.
  • CERT/CC reports that no patch is available and advises Tenda users to disable the remote web management panel and reduce local network exposure.

RedWing MaaS Packages Android Bank Fraud as a Telegram Rental Service — Should Read

RedWing is a new Android malware-as-a-service sold on Telegram that lets low-skill criminals build fake app-store droppers to hijack phones, steal banking credentials, intercept verification codes, and remotely control victims’ devices. Its main defense is preventing sideloading and denying high-risk permissions like Accessibility, default SMS, and battery exemptions to untrusted apps.

  • RedWing is an Android malware operation rented on Telegram as a ready-made bank-fraud service that can take over a victim’s phone, steal banking logins, and capture one-time codes.
  • Zimperium’s zLabs says RedWing appears to be a new variant of Oblivion, a $300-per-month rent-a-malware tool documented earlier this year.
  • Infection begins with a phishing link to a fake app-store page that can mimic Google Play, the Galaxy Store, AppGallery, or custom pages with fake ratings, reviews, and download counts.
  • RedWing abuses Android permissions such as Accessibility, default text-message handler access, notification access, and battery-limit exemptions to read screens, intercept texts, forward calls, stream the screen, log keystrokes, and access device data.
  • Zimperium counted 82 targeted institutions across several sectors, with a strong focus on Russian financial firms, and the operation’s evidence points to the Russian market.

Spain arrests suspected member of pro-Russian hacktivist groups — Should Read

Spanish police arrested a man suspected of supporting pro-Russian hacktivist groups including CyberArmy of Russia Reborn and Z-Pentest, which have been linked to attacks on critical infrastructure. The investigation, launched with FBI information, involved seized computers, frozen crypto wallets, and suspected ties to terrorist organization collaboration and computer damage.

  • Spain's National Police arrested a man suspected of being an active member of the pro-Russian hacktivist groups CyberArmy of Russia Reborn and Z-Pentest.
  • The CyberArmy of Russia Reborn has been linked to cyberattacks against water and food-processing facilities in the U.S., and alleged members have been sanctioned for attacks against SCADA systems of an American energy firm.
  • Spanish police said the arrested individual provided logistical and operational support to a Ukrainian hacker who operated for CARR and attempted to facilitate the hacker’s escape to Russia through Poland and Belarus.
  • The suspect allegedly used encrypted messaging applications to contact other members, coordinate activities, and support operations, including actions attributed to NoName057(16).
  • Authorities raided the suspect’s home in Palencia in March 2026, seized computers and cryptocurrency storage devices, and froze cryptocurrency wallets allegedly used to receive proceeds from sales of stolen data.

Public GitHub Issue Could Trick GitHub Agentic Workflows Into Leaking Private Repo Data — Should Read

Researchers showed that GitHub Agentic Workflows can be manipulated through a public issue to leak private repository contents if the agent has broad read access and can post publicly. The key risk is architectural: AI agents that read untrusted input, access private data, and have an output channel need strict token scoping, isolation, and human review.

  • Noma Security demonstrated a technique called GitLost that can trick GitHub Agentic Workflows into leaking private repository contents through a public GitHub issue.
  • The attack requires no stolen credentials or access to the organization, only the ability to open a normal-looking issue on a public repository that the agent reads.
  • The risk depends on whether the organization has given the agent broad read access across repositories, including private ones, and allows it to post public comments.
  • In Noma Security’s proof of concept, the agent pulled a private repository’s README and pasted it into a public comment after a malicious issue was assigned to the workflow.
  • The article says mitigations include scoping the workflow token to the repository being triaged, limiting what public-facing workflows can post, restricting which authors’ content the agent acts on, and requiring human review of outputs.

The GitHub Actions Attack Pattern Your CI Security Scanners Miss — Should Read

GitHub Actions workflows can be exploitable even when all CI security scans pass, because risks like Cordyceps arise from how multiple valid workflows interact across trust boundaries. The key takeaway is that organizations must govern what enters and runs in their build pipeline, not rely on green scanners as proof of safety.

  • Novee Security disclosed a class of CI/CD weakness called Cordyceps after scanning about 30,000 high-impact repositories and confirming more than 300 as fully exploitable.
  • The article says GitHub Actions workflows using pull_request_target and workflow_run can run in the base repository context with access to secrets and a read/write GITHUB_TOKEN, while acting on attacker-controlled pull request content.
  • The article identifies command injection, JavaScript code injection through actions/github-script, and cross-workflow privilege escalation as the three primitives that enable the attacks.
  • Novee showed that Microsoft’s Azure Sentinel repository could be abused through a pull request comment to run attacker code in Microsoft’s CI and steal a non-expiring GitHub App key, according to the article.
  • The article recommends mitigations including preferring pull_request for untrusted contributions, avoiding checkout of pull request head code in privileged workflows, using read-only default permissions, pinning third-party actions to commit SHAs, and manually approving privileged workflows for first-time contributors.

Rogue Agent Flaw Could Have Let Attackers Hijack Google Dialogflow CX Chatbots — Should Read

A flaw in Google Dialogflow CX, now fixed, could have let someone with edit rights to one Code Block-enabled agent hijack other agents in the same Google Cloud project, read live chats, and inject phishing messages. Google and Varonis say there is no evidence it was exploited.

  • Varonis found a critical flaw in Google Dialogflow CX, named Rogue Agent, that could let an attacker with dialogflow.playbooks.update permission on one Code Block-enabled agent compromise other Code Block-enabled agents in the same Google Cloud project.
  • The flaw affected organizations using Dialogflow Playbooks with custom Code Blocks and was not a remote, unauthenticated attack, making the realistic attacker a malicious insider or someone using a compromised developer account.
  • The issue stemmed from a writable shared file, code_execution_env.py, in a Google-managed Cloud Run environment used by all Code Block-enabled agents in the same Google Cloud project.
  • A successful attacker could read live conversations, exfiltrate user-shared data, and make bots send attacker-written messages such as prompts to re-enter a password.
  • Google fixed the flaw, and both Google and Varonis said there is no evidence it was used in a real attack.

Britain plans to build autonomous AI 'Cyber Shield' to defend nation — Should Read

Britain’s NCSC plans to build “Cyber Shield,” a national AI-powered defense capability using autonomous agents to find and fix weaknesses across government and critical infrastructure networks. The effort aims to keep pace with AI-enabled attackers that can discover vulnerabilities and move far faster than traditional defenses can respond.

  • Britain’s National Cyber Security Centre laid out plans for Cyber Shield, a national-scale sovereign defense capability using agentic AI to discover and fix cybersecurity weaknesses across government networks and critical national infrastructure.
  • The NCSC said AI-aided adversaries can already compress reconnaissance and vulnerability discovery from weeks into minutes, potentially overwhelming traditional defenses.
  • Cyber Shield is planned around paired red and blue AI agents, with red agents probing for weaknesses and blue agents defending systems in real time under the control of the organizations that own them.
  • The NCSC said Cyber Shield will require six core functions, including automated scanning of British networks and fully autonomous fixing of vulnerabilities, with some functions still needing significant research progress.
  • The NCSC attached no timeline to Cyber Shield and invited academia, critical infrastructure operators, frontier AI labs, and the cyber defense sector to help develop the blueprint.

Supreme Court allows Texas app law requiring age verification to take effect — May Read

The Supreme Court is allowing Texas’ App Store Accountability Act, which requires age verification and parental consent for minors downloading apps, to take effect while legal challenges continue. Tech and youth advocacy groups argue the law violates First Amendment rights and forces users to hand over personal data to access online services.

  • The Supreme Court issued an order allowing the Texas App Store Accountability Act to be enforced while a lower court considers the case.
  • The law requires developers and app stores to use age verification tools so children and teens under 18 cannot download apps without parental consent.
  • The Computer and Communications Industry Association, whose members include Google, Meta, and Apple, argues that the law is burdensome and violates the First Amendment.
  • A Texas federal judge put enforcement of the law on hold in December, but an appeals court reinstated it last month.
  • A bipartisan group of more than two dozen state attorneys general filed an amicus brief supporting the Texas law.

How to Set Red Team Objectives that Produce Value — Optional

Red team engagements produce the most value when they start with a single clear, business-relevant objective tied to a decision leadership needs to make. Vague “find what you can” scopes often lead to valid technical findings but weak prioritization and less actionable outcomes.

  • The article argues that a red team engagement is only as useful as the questions it is designed to answer, and that clear objectives help produce root-cause findings leadership can act on.
  • SpecterOps recommends structuring red team engagements around a single primary objective, with secondary objectives pursued only after the primary objective is resolved and tertiary areas explored if time allows.
  • Effective red team objectives should be specific, answerable, actionable, and relevant to actual business risk.
  • The article identifies critical asset reachability, detection coverage validation, response capability testing, and assumption testing as four common categories for valuable red team objectives.
  • Before finalizing an objective, organizations should ask what they would do if the engagement achieved it, because objectives that would not change anything are likely not worth pursuing.
